newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kuwait sets naphtha price for 2.4-2.6 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sets naphtha price for 2.4-2.6 mln tonnes.

text.p: State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) has set naphtha term sales contracts with Asian buyers at $13.50 per tonne over spot Mideast quotes for 2.4-2.6 million tonnes lifting March 1997-February 1998, a company source said on Friday.
"It is the highest premium since at least the liberation of Kuwait," the KPC source told Reuters.

"But we haven't really taken advantage ot the upward trend of the naphtha market. When evaluating the premium, we have taken the end-users' into consideration... the petrochemical situation has not really been in a good situation," he said.
KPC renewed the contracts with 15 buyers from Japan and South Korea and one major, British Petroleum Co Plc, at nearly double the price set in its two rounds of term contracts in 1996.

In last year's contracts, supplies of around 2.6-2.7 million tonnes of the full range naphtha lifting August 1996-September 1997 were set at a $7.90 per tonne premium over Mideast spot quotes, free-on-board Kuwait while March 1996-February 1997 liftings were at $6.50, he said.
The next term talks for the second round of this year's supplies (August 1997-September 1998), is due sometime in June to July in London, he said.
